title: 2020 AMC 10A Problem 21
statement: There exists a unique strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative integers \(a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_k\) such that \[\frac{2^{289}+1}{2^{17}+1}=2^{a_1}+2^{a_2}+\cdots+2^{a_k}.\] What is \(k?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(X=2^{17}\). Then \[ \begin{gathered} \dfrac{2^{289}+1}{2^{17}+1} = \dfrac{X^{17}+1}{X+1} \\ = X^{16}-X^{15}+X^{14} \\ {}-\cdots-X+1 \end{gathered} \].

Pair consecutive terms: \(X^{16}-X^{15}\), \(X^{14}-X^{13}\), \(\ldots\), \(X^2-X\), and then the final \(+1\). Each pair is \(2^{17m}(2^{17}-1)\), contributing \(17\) ones in binary. There are \(8\) such pairs plus the final \(1\), so \(k=8\cdot17+1=137\). Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Pair positive and negative powers to create blocks of binary ones
